intro.text:
Hot water flows along a pipe. Cold water joins from a side branch.

Do they mix?

outro.text:
Fully mixed, it would all be 67 °C. Layering like this matters for thermal stress in pipe junctions.

OpenFOAM buoyantSimpleFoam · 2D RANS

captions.text: Hot water (77 °C) enters from the left. Cold water (27 °C) comes down the branch.
The hot stream is faster and carries more water, so it bends the cold jet over.
The cold water ends up as a layer along the top wall instead of mixing in.
Even at the outlet the water is about 38 °C at the top and 77 °C at the bottom.
